findings.issue: The contract deadlocks ordinary direct-use sessions. It says an agent without a seat is ad hoc and must not take dispatches, then says “No dispatch = no implementation work.” A fresh Claude, Codex, or IDE agent responding directly to its user normally has no hub dispatch, so the canonical contract forbids the work it was opened to do.
findings.suggestion: Scope the dispatch requirement to commissioned seats. Explicitly allow ad-hoc sessions to act on direct user instructions while prohibiting them from consuming seat dispatches.

findings.issue: The routed procedure surface is not usable by Codex in the current repository. There is no `.codex/` tree, while the draft uses Claude-only `/scope`, `/go`, `/check`, `/tds`, and other slash-skill names. Several promised references under `docs/agentic/` do not exist, nor do the claimed nested `AGENTS.md` files. This violates the spec’s one-source/two-runtime requirement and leaves a fresh Codex agent without the procedures the root contract delegates to.
findings.suggestion: Land the shared skill source, generated `.claude/skills` and `.codex/skills` surfaces, referenced documentation, nested contracts, and Claude shims in the same cutover. Use runtime-neutral routing or show both `/name` and `$name`, and add CI that rejects unresolved contract routes.

findings.issue: The sole sanctioned apply path, `scripts/db-apply-guarded.sh`, does not exist. Because the draft simultaneously forbids every other apply path, an agent cannot perform the documented migration workflow.
findings.suggestion: Either ship and test that script in the cutover or point to the real guarded command. Add command-existence validation for executable paths named by the entry contract.

findings.issue: The spec requires session entry to appear here and nowhere else, but the repository still repeats it in `CLAUDE.md` (`Before Working` and `Quick Start`), `docs/PLAYBOOK.md`, the O/I/IMPLEMENTER role templates, and static instructions emitted by `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`. The draft’s cutover note promises removal from only the first two locations.
findings.suggestion: Audit every runtime-loaded boot template and hook during cutover. Remove static session-entry sequences from all of them, leaving only role-specific dynamic context and a pointer to this section. Add the duplicate-heading/content tripwire required by the spec.

findings.issue: The budget is stated incorrectly. The 26 KB limit applies to root plus the deepest nested chain per declared workspace root, not to this file alone. Saying this file may consume 26 KB would allow the repo-owned chain to breach its reserve. The draft also omits exact-separator measurement and launch refusal when global plus repo exceeds `project_doc_max_bytes`.
findings.suggestion: State that the worst-case repo chain is limited to 26 KB and that the exact rendered global-plus-repo payload must remain under the configured runtime ceiling (32768 bytes by default), enforced by CI and the launcher/doctor with a measured breakdown.

findings.issue: The scope classifier compression loses mandatory Standard+ triggers. Current policy includes any migration or new column, major components, foundation data, and workflow/action infrastructure; the draft mentions only new tables/routes/pages, four files, and scenario/factory edits. It also names “classifier config” as the source, but no such authoritative config exists; the workflow contains its own classifier logic.
findings.suggestion: Create and route to one generated classifier source, then include every load-bearing trigger. Until that exists, point to the actual workflow/skill sources and do not imply a nonexistent config is authoritative.

findings.issue: “Haversine or constant fallbacks are NEVER acceptable” contradicts shipped behavior and tests. Scheduler routing intentionally uses a telemetry-marked Haversine tier when Maps/OSRM fail, and `travel-matrix.ts` intentionally uses a 600-second degraded fallback. Issue #3346 concerns refusing to persist fabricated fast-ETA travel times, not a universal ban on degraded routing fallbacks.
findings.suggestion: Scope the prohibition to the affected persistence/fast-ETA path. Preserve the documented scheduler fallbacks with their warning, provenance, and telemetry requirements.

findings.issue: The branch-database label rule is overgeneralized. `epic-db:<ref>` is applied to epic-worktree PRs regardless of whether a particular slice contains a migration, because later slices may depend on the epic branch database. The current non-epic rule is that migration-bearing PRs need isolation; it is not simply “migration means epic-db, everything else no-branch-db.”
findings.suggestion: Define labels by workspace and database target: epic-worktree PRs use their epic DB label; non-epic code-only PRs use `no-branch-db`; migration PRs require an isolated branch DB. Retain the prohibition on using the staging project as an epic DB reference.

findings.issue: “Feature-branch pushes fire NO CI” is false once a PR is open. Multiple workflows subscribe to `pull_request` `synchronize`, so each subsequent feature push reruns PR CI. A fresh agent could create the exact speculative rerun cost the paragraph is trying to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Say that feature pushes trigger no repository CI only before a PR exists; after opening a PR, every push can trigger `synchronize` workflows and should be batched deliberately.

findings.issue: Not every block is correctly tagged or protected. The opening comment contains framework-owned budget, composer, runtime, and routing policy outside forge markers while declaring everything outside markers project-owned. “Nested contracts & exclusions” also mixes Layer-A runtime rules into an unmarked project region.
findings.suggestion: Move every framework-owned block into a named forge region and explicitly tag project-owned blocks as Layer B. Keep mixed subjects in separate regions so composer ownership is unambiguous.

findings.issue: The draft retains procedure bodies that the spec requires routing to skills or docs: the three-layer test authoring recipe and helper APIs, database apply/regeneration sequence, branch-label workflow, local service procedure, and several workspace operations duplicate existing skills and references. This undermines the spec’s single-source and freshness guarantees.
findings.suggestion: Keep only non-negotiable invariants and short gate summaries in the root. Replace operational sequences with verified pointers to their single procedure or reference source.

findings.section: Development Loop and Session Entry commands
findings.issue: The command compression contains commands a fresh agent can misread or cannot run. `msg.sh` has no `hub capture` verb—the durable write verb is `hub finding`—and `scripts/msg.sh hub open|mine` is not a literal valid invocation; `hub mine` also needs sender identity unless `MSG_FROM` is set.
findings.suggestion: Route capture to the `/capture` procedure or name `scripts/msg.sh hub finding`. Show valid alternatives separately, such as `hub open` and `hub mine --from <letter>`.

strongest_aspect: The compact codebase map and many high-risk project facts are well grounded: the project IDs, local-only state files, generated artifacts, test commands, UnifiedOrder deprecation direction, QuickBooks lease requirement, and shared-build constraints match the repository.
biggest_risk: A fresh agent—especially Codex—can be immediately paralyzed or forced to bypass the contract because direct ad-hoc work is forbidden while the delegated Codex skills, documentation targets, nested contracts, and sole database apply command are absent.
